task_summary: Define the interface contract for the 'Routing, Layout & Navigation' component (id: routing_and_layout) of an exemplar.tools documentation website. This includes: ROUTE_SLUG_MAP constant for 14 routes, RouteSlug/RouteEntry/RouteEntryList types, a slug guard utility, Sidebar with NavLinks, Layout with Outlet, and route registration via React Router v6. All in strict TypeScript with vitest tests.

findings.topic: React Router v6 type-safe route definitions
findings.finding: React Router v6 provides createBrowserRouter() which accepts RouteObject[] — each with path, element, and children fields. For a layout-based approach, the Layout component with <Outlet /> is the parent route's element, and all 14 pages are child routes. Using a single ROUTE_ENTRY_LIST as the source of truth allows generating both the sidebar NavLinks and the RouteObject[] from the same data, eliminating drift. The `NavLink` component accepts a `to` prop and provides an `isActive` boolean via its render-prop/className-function signature.
findings.relevance: Directly governs how routes are registered and how the sidebar highlights the active route. Using NavLink's built-in isActive avoids manual location matching.

findings.topic: TypeScript string literal union vs enum for RouteSlug
findings.finding: The canonical registry defines RouteSlug as an enum with 14 variants (leading-slash paths). In TypeScript, this is best modeled as a const object + string literal union (e.g., `export const RouteSlug = { HOME: '/', CARTOGRAPHER: '/cartographer', ... } as const; export type RouteSlug = (typeof RouteSlug)[keyof typeof RouteSlug];`). This gives both runtime values for iteration and compile-time type safety. Native TS enums have known tree-shaking issues with Vite/esbuild and are generally discouraged in modern TS projects — const objects with derived union types are preferred.
findings.source: TypeScript handbook, Matt Pocock patterns, Vite compatibility notes
findings.relevance: Critical for the RouteSlug type definition. Using a const object pattern aligns with named-export-only and composition-over-inheritance operating procedures.

findings.topic: Slug guard utility and double-slash prevention
findings.finding: The operating procedures mandate a slug guard: `slug.startsWith('/') ? slug : '/' + slug`. This must be a pure function with explicit type annotation. Common pitfall: concatenating a base path with a slug that already has a leading slash produces '//step-0'. The guard should also handle edge cases: empty string input, multiple leading slashes ('//foo'), and trailing slashes. A normalize function that trims and deduplicates slashes is more robust: `'/' + slug.replace(/^\/+/, '')` — but the spec is explicit about the ternary form, so use that exactly and add tests for the double-slash scenario.
findings.source: Operating procedures (Slug Handling section), common URL normalization patterns
findings.relevance: Directly required by the contract. Tests must verify no double-slash bugs across all 14 routes.

findings.finding: The canonical registry defines RouteEntry as { stepId: StepId, slug: RouteSlug, label: StepLabel }. RouteEntryList is an ordered array of 14 RouteEntry items defining sidebar order and route registration sequence. This should be a single exported constant (e.g., ROUTE_ENTRY_LIST) that serves as the single source of truth. ROUTE_SLUG_MAP (mentioned in the description) should be derivable from or consistent with this list. The list ordering must match the logical pipeline: Home, Step 0 (Cartographer), Step 1a (Constrain), Step 1b (Ledger), etc.
findings.relevance: Core data structure that both sidebar rendering and route registration consume. Must be exactly 14 entries.

findings.finding: The description specifies ROUTE_SLUG_MAP as a constant mapping all 14 routes with leading-slash values. This should be typed as Record<StepId, RouteSlug> (or a const object with that shape) so that every StepId key maps to exactly one RouteSlug. This enables O(1) lookup by stepId for cross-component navigation (e.g., pipeline diagram nodes clicking through to pages). The values already include leading slashes per operating procedures — the guard utility is for external/dynamic inputs, not for ROUTE_SLUG_MAP values themselves.
findings.source: Operating procedures (Slug Handling), canonical registry (RouteSlug, StepId)
findings.relevance: Primary lookup structure used by other components (pipeline_diagram PipelineNode.slug, page_content navigation).

findings.topic: NavLink active styling with Tailwind CSS
findings.finding: React Router v6 NavLink accepts a className function: `({ isActive }) => isActive ? 'bg-blue-100 font-bold' : 'text-gray-700'`. This is the idiomatic way to highlight the active route in a sidebar. Common pitfall: using `useLocation()` manually and string-comparing paths when NavLink already handles this. Another pitfall: not using `end` prop on the home route NavLink — without it, '/' matches all routes. The home NavLink MUST use `<NavLink to="/" end>` to avoid always being highlighted.
findings.relevance: Directly affects sidebar active-state correctness. The `end` prop on the home route is a frequently missed edge case.

findings.topic: Layout component pattern with React Router Outlet
findings.finding: The standard pattern is: Layout component renders Sidebar + a main content area containing <Outlet />. The router config nests all page routes as children of the Layout route. This ensures sidebar persists across navigation without re-mounting. The Layout should use Tailwind for a flex or grid layout (e.g., `flex h-screen` with sidebar as fixed-width and content as `flex-1 overflow-auto`). The Outlet renders whichever child route matches.
findings.source: React Router v6 layout routes pattern
findings.relevance: Core architectural pattern for the component.

findings.topic: vi.mock() rules for testing routing components
findings.finding: Per operating procedures, vi.mock() factories must provide every named runtime export. When mocking react-router-dom, you must mock NavLink, Outlet, useLocation, etc. — all named exports used. A common pitfall is mocking only the components you think you use and missing one, causing runtime errors in tests. For route existence tests, you can test the data layer (ROUTE_SLUG_MAP, ROUTE_ENTRY_LIST) without mocking React Router at all — pure data tests are preferable. Sidebar rendering tests will need either a MemoryRouter wrapper or mocked NavLink.
findings.relevance: Ensures tests are correct and complete per project standards.

findings.finding: Operating procedures mandate named exports only, no default exports. This means: `export const Layout: React.FC = ...`, `export const Sidebar: React.FC = ...`, `export const ROUTE_SLUG_MAP = ...`, `export const ROUTE_ENTRY_LIST = ...`, `export function ensureLeadingSlash(slug: string): string { ... }`. Type exports use `export type { RouteEntry }`. Each module should have a clear single responsibility. An index.ts barrel file can re-export all public API for the component.
findings.relevance: Structural constraint on all exports from this component.

findings.topic: StepId and StepLabel as const objects with union types
findings.finding: StepId and StepLabel are owned by page_content, not routing_and_layout. However, routing_and_layout consumes them in RouteEntry. The routing component must import these types, not redefine them. If page_content hasn't been implemented yet, the routing component should define its own types only for what it owns (RouteSlug, RouteEntry, RouteEntryList) and import StepId/StepLabel from page_content's contract. If a dependency isn't available yet, a shared types file or the type registry itself should be the import source.
findings.relevance: Prevents type redefinition and ensures cross-component compatibility.

findings.topic: Edge case: trailing slashes and hash fragments
findings.finding: React Router v6 does NOT match trailing slashes by default — '/cartographer/' won't match '/cartographer'. This is rarely a problem for internal navigation but can bite when users type URLs. The optional trailing slash feature was added in React Router v6.14+ with the `trailing` option. For this documentation site, it's safest to not use trailing slashes anywhere in ROUTE_SLUG_MAP and let React Router's default strict matching handle it. No hash-based routing needed since the spec says browser history mode.
findings.source: React Router v6 changelog, common deployment issues
findings.relevance: Edge case that could cause 404s in production if not considered.

findings.finding: The route count (14) must be verified in tests. The registry lists: / (home), /cartographer, /constrain, /ledger, /pact, /advocate, /arbiter, /baton, /sentinel, /chronicler, /stigmergy, /apprentice, /kindex = 13 slugs. Wait — that's only 13. Let me recount: / + 12 step slugs = 13. The description says 'home + 13 steps' = 14. The registry RouteSlug variants list 13 items. StepId has 13 variants (home + 12 steps). StepLabel has 13 variants. This means 13 routes, not 14. The description says 14 but the registry has 13. This discrepancy must be flagged — the contract should match the registry (13 entries).
findings.relevance: Critical: the description says 14 routes but the registry enumerates exactly 13 RouteSlug variants and 13 StepId variants. The contract must resolve this — likely the correct count is 13.

recommended_approach:
Define the routing contract as follows:

1. **Types (owned by routing_and_layout):**
   - `RouteSlug` as a const object + string literal union with all 13 values from the registry (/, /cartographer, /constrain, /ledger, /pact, /advocate, /arbiter, /baton, /sentinel, /chronicler, /stigmergy, /apprentice, /kindex).
   - `RouteEntry` as `{ stepId: StepId; slug: RouteSlug; label: StepLabel }` — exactly matching the registry.
   - `RouteEntryList` as `RouteEntry[]`.
   - Import `StepId` and `StepLabel` from page_content (or a shared types module).

2. **Constants:**
   - `ROUTE_SLUG_MAP`: A `Record<StepId, RouteSlug>` const object providing O(1) stepId→slug lookup. All values include leading slashes.
   - `ROUTE_ENTRY_LIST`: An ordered `RouteEntryList` array of 13 entries defining sidebar order and route registration sequence.

3. **Utility:**
   - `ensureLeadingSlash(slug: string): string` — the specified slug guard using the exact ternary from operating procedures.

4. **Components:**
   - `Sidebar`: Renders NavLinks for all entries in ROUTE_ENTRY_LIST. Uses NavLink's className function for active highlighting. Home NavLink uses `end` prop.
   - `Layout`: Flex container with Sidebar on the left and `<Outlet />` in the main content area. Styled with Tailwind.
   - Route registration in App.tsx: `createBrowserRouter` with Layout as the parent route element and all 13 pages as children, paths derived from ROUTE_ENTRY_LIST.

5. **Tests (vitest):**
   - Verify ROUTE_ENTRY_LIST has exactly 13 entries (matching registry).
   - Verify every ROUTE_SLUG_MAP value starts with '/' and no value produces '//' when used.
   - Verify ensureLeadingSlash handles: already-prefixed, unprefixed, empty string, double-slash input.
   - Verify Sidebar renders 13 NavLinks (one per route) using MemoryRouter wrapper.
   - Verify all RouteSlug values are unique.

6. **Module structure:** Use barrel `index.ts` for clean re-exports. All named exports, `export type {}` for type-only exports.
alternatives_considered: Using native TypeScript enums for RouteSlug — rejected because TS enums have tree-shaking issues with Vite/esbuild and the project prefers const objects with union types.
Using useLocation() + manual path comparison for active sidebar highlighting — rejected in favor of NavLink's built-in isActive which is more idiomatic and less error-prone.
Using HashRouter instead of BrowserRouter — rejected because the spec explicitly requires browser history mode.
Defining StepId and StepLabel inside routing_and_layout — rejected because the canonical registry assigns ownership to page_content. routing_and_layout should import, not redefine.
Using a Map<StepId, RouteSlug> instead of a plain object for ROUTE_SLUG_MAP — rejected because a const object provides better type inference and is more idiomatic in TypeScript.
risks: ROUTE COUNT DISCREPANCY: The component description says '14 routes (home + 13 steps)' but the canonical type registry only defines 13 RouteSlug variants, 13 StepId variants, and 13 StepLabel variants. The contract should use 13 to match the registry. This must be clarified before implementation.

Cross-component type dependency: RouteEntry depends on StepId and StepLabel which are owned by page_content. If page_content hasn't published its types yet, a shared types module or temporary type stubs will be needed to avoid circular dependencies.

NavLink home route over-matching: Without the `end` prop on the home NavLink (to='/'), it will match ALL routes since every path starts with '/'. This is a well-known React Router v6 gotcha that must be explicitly handled.
vi.mock() completeness: If tests mock react-router-dom, every named export used by the component under test must be provided in the mock factory. Missing exports will cause cryptic runtime failures.

Slug guard edge cases: The specified ternary guard `slug.startsWith('/') ? slug : '/' + slug` does NOT handle double-slash inputs like '//foo' or empty strings. Tests should document these known limitations even if the guard isn't extended.
compliance_notes: All source files must be .ts or .tsx — no Python, no .js files.
Strict TypeScript mode — type annotations on all public functions.
Named exports only — no default exports anywhere.
Use `export type { }` for interfaces and type aliases.
vi.mock() factories must provide every named runtime export of mocked modules, with exact export names (ROUTE_SLUG_MAP not ROUTE_SLUGS, etc.).
ROUTE_SLUG_MAP values already include leading slashes — never prepend an extra '/' to values from this map.
Slug guard must use the exact form: `slug.startsWith('/') ? slug : '/' + slug`.
All functions must have at least one test; tests must run without external services.
When importing from sibling modules, use exact exported names — never guess.
Prefer composition over inheritance — no class-based components.
